title: Levi bar Darga
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was very wealthy. Hyman, citing Gittin 45a, relates that he ransomed his daughter, who had been taken captive, for three thousand gold dinars. Abaye said concerning this, “Who can tell us that he acted with the sages' consent?”[^1][^2]

notes.text: Abaye asks whether the sages approved; he does not state categorically that they disapproved.

Hyman supplies three thousand gold dinars. The consulted Gittin 45a instead reads thirteen thousand gold dinars, בתליסר אלפי דינרי זהב. The English attributes the three-thousand account to Hyman and preserves the discrepancy without changing his Hebrew. Abaye questions whether the sages approved and offers the possibility that they did not; this is not a categorical declaration of their disapproval.
